filing_deadline_notes: Benefits capped at 52 weeks from diagnosis date. No benefits beyond 4 years from qualifying event.
notes: Covers salaried firefighters (including special forest wardens, EMS personnel, and fire scene investigators) and volunteer firefighters/EMS. Requires diagnosis by a board-certified psychiatrist or licensed psychologist. Qualifying events, occurring on or after July 1, 2020, include: serious bodily injury or death, incidents involving minors, an immediate life threat, mass casualties, or crime scene investigation. PTSD arising from personnel actions (such as discipline or termination) is excluded. This is not a true rebuttable presumption — it requires diagnosis plus a qualifying event, rather than presuming causation outright; it functions as a compensability pathway. Benefits are capped at 104 weeks from the date of diagnosis, with no award beyond 4 years from the qualifying event. A 2026 causation-reform amendment (Acts 2026, cc. 7, 465), effective January 1, 2027, adds a new qualifying-event category specifically for PTSD — "an incident or exposure without any accompanying physical injury" — removing the prior requirement that a qualifying event involve actual or threatened serious bodily injury or death. This change is not yet in effect.
